chapters.1.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches sincere sharing through a faithful personal example. How does receiving the message amid suffering become an example to others?
chapters.1.summary: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy write to the assembly of the Thessalonians. They thank God for the readers’ faith, love, and enduring hope. The good news came to them in power and in the Holy Spirit. They received the word in much affliction with joy. They became an example to believers in Macedonia and Achaia. People everywhere tell how they turned from idols to serve the living God. They wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised.
chapters.2.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches sharing the gospel with sincerity and love. Why does Paul ask the hearers to remember the teachers' own conduct?
chapters.2.summary: Paul recalls that they came to Thessalonica after being mistreated at Philippi. They did not use flattery or seek glory or money. They were gentle, like a nursing mother with her children. They worked night and day so as not to burden anyone. They urged each one as a father does. The readers accepted the message as God’s word and suffered from their own countrymen. Paul speaks sharply of those in Judea who opposed the assemblies there. He wanted to return, but Satan hindered him, and the readers are his joy.
chapters.3.lds: The selected Church lesson connects increased love with growing holiness. How does Timothy's report give comfort to the teachers as well as the hearers?
chapters.3.summary: Paul could not bear the separation and sent Timothy from Athens. Timothy was to strengthen them so that no one would be shaken by afflictions. Paul had warned them that suffering would come. He feared the tempter had tempted them and the work was wasted. Timothy has now returned with good news of their faith and love. Paul says he lives if they stand firm in the Lord. He prays night and day to see them and supply what their faith lacks. He prays that their love will increase.
chapters.4.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches gradual growth in holiness and work that supports others. Why does the account of the dead end with shared comfort?
chapters.4.summary: Paul urges them to live so as to please God, more and more. God’s will is their holiness, and they are to abstain from sexual immorality. No one should wrong a brother in this matter. They already love one another and should do so more. They should live quietly, mind their own business, and work with their hands. Paul then writes about those who have fallen asleep. The dead in Christ will rise first, when the Lord descends with a shout. Then the living will be caught up to be with the Lord always.
chapters.5.lds: How do different needs require different kinds of care?
chapters.5.summary: Paul says they need no letter about times and seasons. The day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night. They are children of light and should stay awake and sober. They wear faith and love as a breastplate and hope as a helmet. They should respect those who labor among them and lead them. Paul gives short commands: rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in everything. They should not quench the Spirit, and they should test all things. He asks that the letter be read to all the brothers.
